findings.title: on_delete is hardcoded to "cancel" even though the module supports streaming pipelines
findings.explanation: on_delete controls what terraform destroy/replace does to the job: "cancel" terminates immediately, dropping any in-flight and buffered records; "drain" lets a streaming job finish processing what it has already ingested before stopping. The module exposes enable_streaming_engine, so it explicitly supports streaming jobs, but on_delete is hardcoded to "cancel" with no way for a caller to opt into "drain". Any streaming pipeline built with this module will lose in-flight data on every terraform destroy or replacement (e.g. a template_gcs_path or network change that forces recreation).
findings.remediation: Expose on_delete as a variable (default "cancel" to preserve current behavior for batch jobs) with validation restricting it to ["drain", "cancel"], and document that streaming jobs should set it to "drain".
